one_line: Defenders of Bhatner and Delhi facing Timur’s 1398 invasion of north India.

appearance.age_look: Rao Daljit appears in his early 30s with a lean, battle-trained build, while Sultan Mahmud Tughlaq looks in his late 20s with a royal yet tense bearing.
appearance.face: Rao Daljit has a sharp oval face, wheatish-brown Rajasthani complexion, a straight nose, trimmed moustache and short boxed beard, with intense, determined eyes and a default expression of grim resolve; Mahmud Tughlaq has a slightly broader oval face, medium-brown north Indian complexion, neatly groomed moustache and short beard, thoughtful eyes with faint under-eye shadows, and a default expression of dignified worry and restrained anger.
appearance.hair: Rao Daljit’s black hair is tied into a short warrior’s knot at the back of his head, mostly hidden beneath a deep-red quilted turban-style pagri with a narrow mustard border and a small central bronze disc; Mahmud Tughlaq’s black hair is cropped short under a dark indigo cloth-wrapped conical helmet with a mail aventail and a small brass finial at the crown.
appearance.costume: Rao Daljit wears a long-sleeved, knee-length quilted cotton coat (patka-style paadded tunic) in muted marigold yellow with narrow crimson vertical edging, worn over a dull steel mail shirt that peeks at the sleeves and hem; a deep-red cotton sash is tied firmly around his waist, with the loose end hanging on his left; he has straight, off-white cotton churidar trousers gathered tightly at the calves, and dark brown leather boots reaching mid-calf; his forearms are protected by simple brown leather bracers with stitching visible; a plain bronze kara-style bangle circles his right wrist, and small stud earrings glint at his ears, adding subtle Rajasthani detail; Mahmud Tughlaq wears a dark indigo, long-sleeved, knee-length kufani-style tunic of sturdy cloth under a sleeveless lamellar cuirass of overlapping dull steel plates laced with dark leather, the armour slightly curved over his torso; a broad olive-green cloth belt wraps his waist, securing a sheathed dagger; his lower body is covered with loose, straight-cut grey cotton trousers, tucked into black leather riding boots that reach just below the knee; a simple dark-cream scarf is draped once around his shoulders and back, hinting at royal dignity even in the field; his overall costume remains modest, fully covering torso and legs in historically plausible, late-14th-century north Indian court-military style.
appearance.signature: Rao Daljit carries a long, slightly curved Indian talwar with a steel blade, a brass hilt and a distinctive disc pommel, its plain dark-brown scabbard hanging from his red waist sash, while Mahmud Tughlaq grips a slender, slightly curved cavalry spear with a leaf-shaped steel head and a polished dark-wood shaft about his own height.

ref_desc: Rao Daljit has a wheatish oval face with moustache and short beard, black hair in a knot under a deep-red pagri, wearing a marigold quilted coat over mail, off-white churidar and brown boots with a brass-hilt talwar, while Mahmud Tughlaq has a medium-brown oval face, short beard, indigo cloth-wrapped conical helm, dark indigo tunic under steel lamellar, grey trousers, black boots and an olive belt, both in marigold yellow, deep red, indigo blue, steel grey and olive green tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet showing Rao Daljit and Sultan Mahmud Tughlaq standing side by side as defenders during Timur’s 1398 invasion: Rao Daljit is a lean early-30s Rajput noble with a wheatish oval face, straight nose, trimmed moustache and short boxed beard, intense eyes and a grimly resolved expression; his black hair is tied in a short knot under a deep-red quilted pagri with a narrow mustard border and a small central bronze disc. He wears a long-sleeved, knee-length marigold yellow quilted cotton coat with narrow crimson vertical edging over a dull steel mail shirt that shows at the sleeves and hem, a deep-red cotton sash tied at his waist with the loose end hanging on his left, straight off-white cotton churidar trousers gathered at the calves, and dark brown leather boots to mid-calf; his forearms have plain brown leather bracers and a simple bronze kara bangle on his right wrist, with small stud earrings. At his left hip hangs his signature weapon, a long, slightly curved Indian talwar with a steel blade, brass hilt and disc pommel in a plain dark-brown scabbard. Beside him, Sultan Mahmud Tughlaq is a late-20s north Indian sultan with a medium-brown oval face, neat moustache and short beard, thoughtful eyes with faint under-eye shadows and a dignified yet worried expression; his black hair is cropped under a dark indigo cloth-wrapped conical helmet with a mail aventail and small brass finial. He wears a dark indigo long-sleeved kufani-style tunic of sturdy cloth under a sleeveless dull-steel lamellar cuirass of overlapping plates laced with dark leather, a broad olive-green cloth belt securing a sheathed dagger, loose straight grey cotton trousers tucked into black leather riding boots just below the knee, and a simple dark-cream scarf draped once around his shoulders; he holds his signature slender, slightly curved cavalry spear with a leaf-shaped steel head and polished dark-wood shaft. Keep both fully and modestly clothed in historically plausible late-14th-century north Indian military styles with dominant colours of marigold yellow, deep red, indigo blue, steel grey and olive green, and present them front-facing and three-quarter views to clearly show face, hair, armour, garments and weapons.
